evals.prompt: Draw a diagram of a web app: a load balancer in front of two web servers that both talk to one Postgres database. I want to watch it in my browser.
evals.expected_output: Runs `status` or `start` and gives the user the canvas URL, creates shapes with custom ids and bound arrows in one `add` or `apply`, then runs `describe` to check the layout.
expectations: Runs commands through `uv run --script <skill-dir>/scripts/cli.py`, not bare `bun x` or browser automation
Gives the user the canvas URL
Creates four labeled shapes with custom ids in one batch call

evals.prompt: I just moved some boxes around on the excalidraw canvas and renamed the cache box. Make the cache box red and connect it to the API box.
evals.expected_output: Runs `describe` first to read the current scene, finds both elements by id or label, then updates color and adds a bound arrow with `apply` or `update` plus `add`.
expectations: Targets elements by id, not by coordinates
Uses a red stroke and fill pair
Adds an arrow bound to both element ids

evals.prompt: Save the current excalidraw diagram into docs/architecture.excalidraw in this repo, then wipe the canvas so I can start something new.
evals.expected_output: Exports to the requested path before clearing, and saves a snapshot or relies on the export before running `clear --yes`.

evals.prompt: Take a screenshot of the excalidraw canvas so you can check the arrows look right.
evals.expected_output: Runs `screenshot --out` to a temp path; on exit code 4 asks the user to open the canvas URL instead of opening a browser itself.
expectations: On exit code 4, asks the user to open the canvas URL
Does not launch or drive a browser itself
